statement: A resolver that must bind a runtime/agent identifier to a row in a DIFFERENT identity-bearing table (e.g. a CRM persona, a wallet persona, a registry asset) MUST walk a named, documented canonical chain of foreign-key/unique-constraint hops end to end. When no row exists at the end of that chain, the resolver MUST provision a NEW row under a distinct, collision-proof namespace marker (e.g. a dedicated app_origin/source tag) rather than adopting an existing row selected by fuzzy match (name similarity, partial identifier match, heuristic 'closest' row) or fabricating an identifier that was never actually issued. A resolver that cannot complete the chain returns `undefined`/`null` (three-valued: unresolved vs. genuinely absent), never a guessed value.
classification: A No-Guessing violation at the identity-resolution layer: querying a UUID-backed column with a text runtime id (or, more generally, matching an identity row by plausibility rather than by a real foreign-key chain) silently fails closed (resolves nothing) or, worse, could silently bind to the wrong principal if a fuzzy match were used instead. The generic shape is any cross-table identity lookup authored against an assumed schema rather than the actual documented chain of keys.

canaries.assertion: resolveAgentStandingPersonaId walks agent_root_identity.did_uri -> personas.root_did -> personas.id -> crm_personas.identity_persona_id -> crm_personas.id; when no canonical persona exists it provisions one under app_origin = 'aigent-canonical-standing' rather than matching an existing ambiguous row; a failed read at any hop returns undefined, never a fabricated id.

occurrences.defect: resolveAgentStandingPersonaId queried crm_personas.identity_persona_id (UUID-backed) using the text runtime agent id (e.g. 'aigent-nakamoto') directly — a query shape that can never match, so every agent's Standing persona resolved to nothing regardless of whether a real Standing score existed, silently blocking Runtime eligibility (score >= 25) and Authority BOUNDED/ACTIVE derivation.

notes: A specialization of inv.engineering.036/037 (one authoritative location per concern) applied to IDENTITY RESOLUTION specifically: the canonical chain is the one authoritative path from a runtime agent id to its CRM Standing persona, and any resolver that re-derives its own shortcut (assumed column semantics, name-similarity match) risks drifting from — or silently binding the wrong identity to — that path.

The provisioning half of this invariant (create-under-a-distinct-namespace-marker rather than adopt-an-ambiguous-row) generalizes beyond Standing personas to any 'first touch creates the canonical record' resolver pattern in this codebase — e.g. AigentQube registry-asset provisioning already follows the same shape (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE against a fixed, namespaced asset_id, never a fuzzy match against existing rows).
